newsitem.title: USA: Albright says considering trip to South Asia.
newsitem.headline: Albright says considering trip to South Asia.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright said on Tuesday she was considering a trip to South Asia to mark this year's 50th anniversary of the independence of India and Pakistan.
Albright, speaking to reporters before talks with Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan, gave no dates for the possible trip.
"I am considering a trip to the region. This is the 50th anniversary of independence and it seems to be an appropriate time for a trip to be planned," Albright said.

British India was divided into predominantly Hindu India and predominantly Moslem Pakistan when the British withdrew in 1947. The eastern part of Pakistan later became the separate country of Bangladesh.

Albright said she would be seeking a briefing from Ayub Khan on the outcome of the Indo-Pakistani summit in the Maldives last week, a meeting that she said had been "very important and useful" in improving the two countries' ties.
The main issue dividing India and Pakistan is Kashmir. Albright said a dialogue between the countries on Kashmir "would be very useful and would be terrific to resolve this."
